target.title: fix(ui): keep submitted prompts visible during active runs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a newly submitted prompt could disappear from the Control UI while its agent run was active after a page reload or Gateway reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The durable queue persists `sendAttempts` but intentionally does not persist the page-local `performance.now()` submission timestamp. The chat thread now treats a persisted send attempt as proof that transport started, while retaining the existing allowed-state restrictions so unsent reconnect-waiting and steerable queued prompts stay above the composer.

## User Impact

Submitted prompts remain visible in the chat thread while the agent is working, including across reload/reconnect recovery, and remain present when the final response arrives.

## Evidence

- Focused unit regression: 102 tests passed in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts`.
- Mocked Gateway browser flow: `stores new input while offline and sends it after reconnect` passed with the prompt visible beside the active Stop control before the final response (`run_5eec47f9de4e`).
- Production Control UI build passed on the same source content (`run_6a42da1abdf8`).
- Focused formatting and lint passed (`run_743cf1bb92e4`).
- Two autoreview passes reported no accepted/actionable findings; final branch review rated the patch correct.

Behavior addressed: A submitted prompt disappeared while its run was active after reload/reconnect recovery.

Real environment tested: Linux AWS Crabbox with Chromium, the production Vite build, and a mocked Gateway WebSocket exercising offline queue persistence and reconnect.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts -t 'stores new input while offline and sends it after reconnect'`

Evidence after fix: The focused E2E passed and captured offline-queued, reconnected-active, and delivered states; the focused unit file and production build also passed.

Observed result after fix: The user prompt remains rendered in the thread while Stop generating is visible, then remains in history after the Gateway final event.

What was not tested: Cross-browser engines beyond Chromium; no provider credentials or external channels are involved in this Control UI state transition.
